newsitem.title: USA: Daiwa says glad to settle CBOT violation charges.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa says glad to settle CBOT violation charges.

text.p: Daiwa Bank Ltd said Tuesday it was pleased to have settled rules violation charges with the Chicago Board of Trade.
"The bank is pleased to have settled this matter with the CBOT, which arose out of the trading activities of the convicted felon Toshihide Iguchi," the bank's U.S. spokesman said.
Last December, a federal district court in New York sentenced Iguchi, a former Daiwa trader, to four years in prison for his role in a $1.1 billion trading scandal.

Daiwa was forced to halt its U.S. operations in February 1996 because of the scandal, which involved a coverup of a $1.1 billion loss from trading in U.S. bonds. A three-year ban on its operating in the U.S. runs until February 1999.
Earlier, the CBOT said Daiwa agreed to pay a $60,000 fine without admitting or denying any violations.
